content:
h08.

Two types declare `RunOnce`, both `*Runner` types in separate runner packages:

**`memopayload.Runner.RunOnce`** — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — **not invoked** — no caller. The map returns a certified zero for its call sites, and a whole-repo text search for `RunOnce` finds only the declaration and doc comment (lines 26–27) — no reference in production *or* test code. It is effectively dead entry point for a memo-payload rebuild backfill.

**`s3presign.Runner.RunOnce`** — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — **invoked, from two production call sites**:
- `s3presign.Runner.Run` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (the ticker loop, one call per tick)
- `server.Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `server/server.go:163` (a single eager pass at startup, immediately before the continuous `Run` goroutine is launched at line 165)

Answer format:

| declarer | invoked? | caller(path) |
|---|---|---|
| `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`) | no | — (certified zero; no test callers either) |
| `s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43`) | yes | `s3presign.Runner.Run` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`); `server.Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:163`) |

The asymmetry is the notable part: the s3presign runner follows a "run once at boot, then on a ticker" pattern wired into `startBackgroundRunners`, while the memopayload runner exposes the same shape of API but was never wired into server startup — so its `RunOnce` has no path to execution as the code stands.
